reasons: Uses a real match file and checks specific scores and timings.
Covers repeatability, resume, and error codes.
Edge cases such as an empty header are tested directly.

terms.meaning: One step of a replay, such as one ball, with its time and the running score.
A way for a server to keep sending updates to a browser over one open connection.
A header a browser sends to say which update it last received, so the stream can continue from there.
How many times faster than real time the replay runs. At 60 times speed, 30 seconds of match time takes half a second.
A web address the app answers on, here the replay address for an event.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loads the 2008 match for replay
sections.what: Resets the test database and loads the 2008 KKR v RCB match as the test event, with each ball timed 30 seconds after the last.
sections.why: Likely reason: a real, fixed match gives predictable frames and scores to check against.
sections.watch_out: The expected scores are tied to this match file, so a new version of the file will break the score checks.

sections.name: read
sections.title: Reads a streamed response
sections.what: Takes a streamed text response and splits it into separate events, so each event's id, type and data can be checked.
sections.why: Likely reason: streamed text is hard to check directly, so tests turn it into a simple list.
sections.watch_out: The splitter assumes each field fits on one line and the data is JSON. Multi-line data would be read incorrectly.

sections.name: incident replay (replay)
sections.title: Checks the replay feed and endpoint
sections.what: Checks that frames are timed on the replay clock, the running score per innings matches the match, planning is repeatable, and the stream waits between frames and resumes after a given id. Also checks the web endpoint returns an event stream, returns 404 for unknown events, and returns 400 for an invalid speed.
sections.why: Likely reason: a replay must match the real match, run at the chosen speed, and recover from a dropped connection.
sections.watch_out: An empty Last-Event-ID header must mean start from the beginning. The test guards this edge, so changes to header handling could skip the first frame silently.

summary: Tests the match replay feature: it plans timed frames from a real match, streams them as server-sent events, resumes after a dropped connection, and validates the web endpoint.
purpose: Makes sure a replay is repeatable, runs at the chosen speed, can resume where it stopped, and rejects bad requests.
why: Likely reason: replays are streamed to the browser, so they must be repeatable and resumable when a connection drops. Reason not stated in the code for every test.
how: Loads the 2008 KKR v RCB match into the test database with fixed timestamps. Plans frames on a replay clock, dividing the gap between balls by the speed. Checks the running score for each innings. Streams frames with a wait between them, and resumes from the last event id. Finally calls the web endpoint and checks its status codes and headers.
inputs: A saved Cricsheet match file for 2008 KKR v RCB, the speed setting, and a last event id from the request header.
outputs: A list of timed frames, a stream of server-sent events ending with an end event, and HTTP status codes 200, 400 or 404.
risks: Expected scores are tied to this match file, so a new version of the fixture breaks them. An empty last-event-id header is treated as a fresh start, which is a subtle edge.
debug: If a replay test fails, check the planned frame times first. Then check the score totals against the match file. For stream problems, read the raw text the stream produces.
